title: Choose the visual world
question: The re-roll assigned The Plate Archive. Keep it, take the alternate, or re-roll again.

options.label: The Plate Archive
options.lineage: observatory glass-plate archives and their ink-annotated measurements
options.thesis: Her work as an observatory's plate archive: every object catalogued, measured and annotated in ink; nothing claimed that isn't on the plate.
materials: bevelled glass plates with silver emulsion
options.viewport: One large glass plate holding her portrait in silver grain, four objects circled in ink and labelled Full-stack, Mobile, Web3, AI-driven engineering; beside it the kraft envelope with catalogue number, her name and 'Plate log: CV (PDF)'.
options.risk: Drifts into a generic space theme if any annotation is decorative rather than real data.

raised.raise: State is drawn by ink stroke, never colour: solid circle shipped, dashed in development, double ring case study.
Every plate has a catalogue number that is also its address (/plate/014), and ⌘K takes numbers.
One type family across the archive; hierarchy comes from case, indentation and rules.
Exactly one annotation per view may break the plate grid: the most important fact on it.
Sections are discrete plates stacked with deep, constant gaps; measurements always sit on the plate edge.
One axis carries time: plates file along a single dated spine, newest first.

options.label: Four Lines
options.lineage: metro line diagrams and enamel station signage
options.thesis: Her career as a transit diagram: four coloured lines for her four areas, stations for projects and roles, interchanges where work crosses areas.
options.viewport: Her name as the map title; four lines run in and meet at a 'Now: Wandity' interchange; every station is a project or role you can open.
options.risk: Familiar: transit-map résumés are a known infographic trope and can read as a CV template.

options.label: Jackfield Schedule
options.thesis: Projects as numbered amber lanes with link-line states.
options.viewport: 48 numbered lanes under a legend strip.
options.case: Fuses poorly: an operator's console recruiters don't identify with, and dense lanes bury the four areas.
options.kept: State drawn by stroke pattern, never colour.

options.label: Teletext Pages
options.thesis: Every section a numbered teletext page.
options.case: Fuses poorly: retro novelty, and block mosaics can't show project screenshots.

options.label: Phosphor Terminal
options.thesis: The portfolio as a typed transcript.
options.viewport: A blinking cursor and an 80-column transcript.
options.case: Fuses poorly: exactly the developer costume ruled out in the brief.
options.kept: One face; hierarchy by case, indentation and rules.

options.label: Layout Desk
options.thesis: Colliding type you feel before you read.
options.viewport: Three overlapping headlines over a photo.
options.case: Fuses poorly: deliberately hard to read, the opposite of a ten-second shortlist.
options.kept: Break the grid only where the content is most urgent.

options.label: Cloud Quarry
options.thesis: Projects cut as blocks of weather.
options.viewport: A cloud cliff with a saw line.
options.case: Fuses poorly: surreal and light-ground, against the audience and dark-only.
options.kept: Measurements on tally edges; deep constant gaps between blocks.

options.label: Rain Nocturne
options.thesis: The portfolio as a city lighting up.
options.case: Fuses poorly: atmosphere without a place for proof; neon on dark is the AI-default look.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark developer portfolio as the category ships it, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Name and role headline, short intro, buttons, then a grid of project cards.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other developer portfolios by design.
